common_name: Blue Sprite Speedwell (Compact Chicagoland Grows Veronica)

planting.note: Plant divisions or container stock in spring in well-drained soil in full sun, where the clump will knit together into a tidy flowering mat by its second season.

directions: Blue Sprite is one of several compact Veronica selections bred through the Chicagoland Grows cooperative program run by the Chicago Botanic Garden, Morton Arboretum, and regional growers, producing upright spikes of small blue flowers over a low, spreading mat of foliage. Plant in average, well-drained garden soil in full sun and divide every few years to keep the clump vigorous. It works well edging a sunny perennial border or rock garden and tolerates brief dry spells once established.

common_name: Bad Hair Day Switchgrass (Fine-Textured Chicagoland Grows Panicum)

planting.note: Plant divisions in spring in average to dry soil in full sun, cutting the prior season's blades back hard before new growth emerges.

directions: Bad Hair Day is a switchgrass selection introduced through Chicagoland Grows, named for its airy, tousled seedheads that rise above an upright clump of narrow blades through summer and fall. As a warm-season native grass it tolerates heat, drought, and clay soils once rooted in, making it low-maintenance in a sunny border or naturalistic planting. Cut the whole clump back to a few inches in late winter before new shoots appear, and divide it when the center starts to thin.

common_name: Pink Cotton Candy Betony (Chicagoland Grows Stachys)

planting.note: Plant in well-drained soil in full sun to light shade in spring, giving the clump room to spread into a low mat.

directions: Pink Cotton Candy is a Chicagoland Grows Stachys selection valued for dense spikes of pink flowers held above a low mound of foliage, drawing bees through the summer. Grow it in average, well-drained soil in full sun to light afternoon shade, where it forms a tidy groundcover at the front of a border. Shear off spent flower spikes to tidy the clump and encourage a second flush.

common_name: Lavender Rose Prairieblues Baptisia (Bicolor Lavender-and-Rose False Indigo Hybrid)

planting.note: Plant container stock in spring in well-drained soil in full sun on a permanent site, since Baptisia's deep taproot resents later transplanting.

directions: Lavender Rose is a Prairieblues-series false indigo bred through the Chicagoland Grows program at the Chicago Botanic Garden, carrying bicolor lavender-and-rose pea-like flower spikes above blue-green foliage in late spring. Site it in full sun in well-drained, average soil and choose a permanent spot, since the plant develops a deep taproot and does not divide or transplant well once mature. Once established it is extremely drought-tolerant and functions almost like a small flowering shrub, needing only an occasional late-winter cutback.

common_name: Billowing Violet Aromatic Aster (Chicagoland Grows Violet Aster)

planting.note: Plant in average, well-drained soil in full sun in spring, giving the mound room to billow outward by fall.

directions: Billowing Violet is a compact aromatic aster from the Chicagoland Grows program, forming a low, rounded mound that disappears under violet daisy flowers in autumn when little else in the garden is blooming. Like its sibling selections in the Billowing series, it tolerates heat, drought, and poor soil once rooted in, and its dense habit needs no staking. Cut the mound back hard in late winter to keep next year's growth compact and floriferous.

common_name: Perfectly Puzzling Creeping Phlox (Patterned Petal Chicagoland Grows Phlox)

planting.note: Plant in gritty, well-drained soil in full sun to light shade in spring, spacing plants to knit into a mat within a season or two.

directions: Perfectly Puzzling is a low, mat-forming hybrid phlox bred through the Chicagoland Grows program, carrying an intricately patterned petal face that stands out from solid-colored creeping phlox. Grow it in well-drained soil in sun to light shade, where it spreads into a dense evergreen carpet suited to rock gardens, walls, and border edges. Shear lightly after the main spring flush to tidy the mat and occasionally encourage rebloom.

common_name: Running With Scissors Creeping Phlox (Fringed-Petal Chicagoland Grows Phlox)

planting.note: Plant in gritty, well-drained soil in full sun to light shade in spring, where the mat will spread over nearby rocks or edging.

directions: Running With Scissors is a creeping phlox selection from the Chicagoland Grows program noted for its irregularly cut, almost jagged-edged petals, a playful departure from the smooth-edged blooms typical of the species. It forms a low, evergreen mat best suited to full sun or light shade in sharply drained soil, making it a good choice for rock gardens and slopes. Shear back lightly once flowering fades to keep the mat dense and encourage fresh growth.

common_name: Tough Love Spiderwort (Resilient Chicagoland Grows Tradescantia)

planting.note: Plant divisions in spring in average, moisture-retentive soil in full sun to part shade.

directions: Tough Love is a Chicagoland Grows spiderwort bred for garden durability, opening three-petaled flowers each morning atop grassy, arching clumps through much of the summer. Plant it in full sun to part shade in soil that holds moisture, and shear the whole clump back by half after the first bloom flush to refresh its foliage and trigger repeat flowering. It tolerates both heavy clay and brief dry spells, living up to its name as a dependable perennial.

common_name: Mojito Prairieblues Baptisia (Chartreuse-Accented False Indigo Hybrid)

planting.note: Plant container stock in spring in well-drained soil in full sun on a permanent site, since Baptisia's deep taproot resents later transplanting.

directions: Mojito is a Prairieblues-series false indigo from the Chicagoland Grows program, its name nodding to the fresh, lime-tinged tones that run through its flower spikes above blue-green foliage in late spring. Grow it in full sun in well-drained soil and pick a permanent location, as the plant's deep taproot makes it a poor candidate for later moves or division. Once settled it is drought-tolerant and essentially self-sufficient, needing little beyond an annual late-winter cutback.

common_name: Blue Mound Prairieblues Baptisia (Compact Mounding Blue False Indigo)

planting.note: Plant container stock in spring in well-drained soil in full sun on a permanent site, since Baptisia's deep taproot resents later transplanting.

directions: Blue Mound is a more compact Prairieblues false indigo from the Chicagoland Grows program, forming a dense, rounded clump of blue-green foliage topped with blue flower spikes in late spring rather than the taller, looser habit of many Baptisia. Its tidier size suits smaller borders where full-size Baptisia would overwhelm the space. Site it in full sun in well-drained soil on a permanent spot, since it shares the genus's deep taproot and resents being moved once established.

common_name: Pink Parasol Creeping Phlox (Chicagoland Grows Pink-Flowered Phlox)

planting.note: Plant in gritty, well-drained soil in full sun to light shade in spring, allowing room for the mat to spread.

directions: Pink Parasol is a creeping phlox from the Chicagoland Grows breeding program, blanketing itself in clear pink flowers each spring over a low, evergreen mat of needle-like foliage. Grow it in sharply drained soil in full sun to light shade, where it is well suited to rock gardens, slopes, and border edges. A light shearing after bloom keeps the mat tight and can coax a modest second flush of flowers.

common_name: Plumtastic Creeping Phlox (Plum-Purple Chicagoland Grows Phlox)

planting.note: Plant in gritty, well-drained soil in full sun to light shade in spring, allowing room for the mat to spread.

directions: Plumtastic is a Chicagoland Grows creeping phlox selected for rich plum-purple flowers held over a dense, low evergreen mat. It thrives in sharply drained soil in full sun to light shade and is well suited to rock gardens, walls, and the front of a sunny border. Shear the mat lightly after its main spring bloom to keep it compact and tidy through summer.

common_name: Tidal Pool Speedwell (Chicagoland Grows Veronica)

planting.note: Plant divisions or container stock in spring in well-drained soil in full sun, giving the low mat room to spread.

directions: Tidal Pool is a low, spreading Veronica from the Chicagoland Grows program, forming a dense groundcover mat studded with small blue flower spikes through late spring and early summer. Plant it in average, well-drained soil in full sun, where it works well cascading over a wall edge or filling gaps between pavers. Divide the clump every few years to maintain vigor and prevent the center from thinning.

common_name: Summer's End Narrowleaf Ironweed (Late-Season Chicagoland Grows Vernonia)

planting.note: Plant in average to lean, well-drained soil in full sun in spring, where the fine-textured clump will fill in by its second year.

directions: Summer's End is a compact narrowleaf ironweed from the Chicagoland Grows program, closing out the growing season with clusters of rosy-purple flowers above finely textured, almost thread-like foliage. Like its sibling selections in the same breeding line, it tolerates heat and drought once established and draws butterflies heavily in its late bloom window. Grow it in full sun in lean, well-drained soil and cut the clump back in late winter before new growth starts.

common_name: Verdant Venture Blue Star (Chicagoland Grows Amsonia Hybrid)

planting.note: Plant in average, well-drained soil in full sun to part shade in spring, allowing room for the clump to fill out over several seasons.

directions: Verdant Venture is an interspecific Amsonia hybrid from the Chicagoland Grows program, opening clusters of soft blue star-shaped flowers in late spring over foliage that turns a clear gold in autumn. Once established it is deeply drought-tolerant and rarely needs dividing, forming an attractive, shrub-like clump for a sunny or lightly shaded border. Cut the stems back in late winter before new shoots emerge to keep the planting tidy.

common_name: Summer Snow Boneset (White-Flowered Chicagoland Grows Eupatorium)

planting.note: Plant in moisture-retentive soil in full sun to part shade in spring, giving the clump adequate room to reach full size.

directions: Summer Snow is a Eupatorium selection from the Chicagoland Grows program, covering itself in flat clusters of small white flowers in late summer that are heavily visited by bees and butterflies. Grow it in soil that stays reliably moist, in full sun to part shade, where its upright clump adds late-season interest to a border or rain garden. Cut the stems back in late winter and divide the clump every few years to keep it vigorous.

common_name: Early Bird Creeping Phlox (Early-Blooming Chicagoland Grows Phlox)

planting.note: Plant in gritty, well-drained soil in full sun to light shade in spring, allowing room for the mat to spread.

directions: Early Bird is a Chicagoland Grows creeping phlox selected to open its flowers ahead of most other cultivars in the series, giving an earlier burst of color over its low evergreen mat. Grow it in sharply drained soil in full sun to light shade, where it suits rock gardens, walls, and border edges. Shear the mat lightly once the main flush fades to keep growth dense through the rest of the season.

common_name: Cotton Candy Aromatic Aster (Pastel Pink Chicagoland Grows Aster)

planting.note: Plant in average, well-drained soil in full sun in spring, giving the mound room to fill out by fall.

directions: Cotton Candy is a Chicagoland Grows aromatic aster with soft pastel pink flowers covering a dense, rounded mound in autumn. It shares the drought tolerance and compact, self-supporting habit of its sibling selections in the same breeding line, needing no staking even in exposed sites. Grow it in full sun in well-drained soil and cut the mound back hard in late winter to keep next season's growth tight.

common_name: Pride of Georgia Wall Germander (Evergreen Chicagoland Grows Teucrium)

planting.note: Plant in lean, well-drained soil in full sun in spring, where the low subshrub will knit into a tidy edging.

directions: Pride of Georgia is a wall germander selection from the Chicagoland Grows program, forming a neat, semi-evergreen low hedge of glossy leaves topped with purple-pink flower spikes in summer. Site it in lean, sharply drained soil in full sun, where its drought tolerance makes it useful for edging paths or borders without constant watering. Trim lightly after flowering to maintain a crisp, uniform shape.

common_name: Blue Lime Switchgrass (Blue-Green Chicagoland Grows Panicum)

planting.note: Plant divisions in spring in average to dry soil in full sun, cutting last year's growth back before new shoots appear.

directions: Blue Lime is a switchgrass selection from the Chicagoland Grows program, its cool blue-green blades standing upright through summer before airy seedheads open above the clump in fall. As a warm-season native grass it handles heat, drought, and heavy soils with ease once established, needing little more than an annual cutback. Grow it in full sun for the strongest blade color and to keep the clump from flopping.

common_name: Forever Pink Creeping Phlox (Long-Blooming Chicagoland Grows Phlox)

planting.note: Plant in gritty, well-drained soil in full sun to light shade in spring, allowing room for the mat to spread.

directions: Forever Pink is a Chicagoland Grows creeping phlox chosen for an extended pink bloom period that outlasts many of its series-mates, forming a low evergreen mat in sun or light shade. Plant it in sharply drained soil for best results, since soggy ground in winter can rot the crown. Shear the mat lightly after the main flush fades to keep it dense and tidy for the rest of the season.

common_name: Fire Marshall Bee Balm (Red-Flowered Chicagoland Grows Monarda)

planting.note: Plant in average, well-drained soil in full sun in spring, with good air circulation to limit powdery mildew.

directions: Fire Marshall is a bee balm hybrid from the Chicagoland Grows program bred for strong resistance to powdery mildew alongside vivid red, hummingbird-attracting flowers through summer. Grow it in full sun in average soil with reasonable air movement around the clump to keep foliage clean late into the season. Divide every few years to maintain vigor and deadhead spent flower heads to extend the bloom window.

common_name: Burgundy Fireworks Coneflower (Dark Red Chicagoland Grows Echinacea)

planting.note: Plant in average, well-drained soil in full sun in spring, where the clump will bulk up over its first two seasons.

directions: Burgundy Fireworks is a coneflower selection from the Chicagoland Grows program, carrying deep burgundy-red petals around a prominent central cone through the summer. Grow it in full sun in well-drained soil; once established it tolerates heat and drought with ease and draws pollinators and seed-eating finches alike. Leave spent flower heads standing into winter for the birds, then cut the clump back in early spring.

common_name: Pink Profusion Creeping Phlox (Heavy-Blooming Chicagoland Grows Phlox)

planting.note: Plant in gritty, well-drained soil in full sun to light shade in spring, allowing room for the mat to spread.

directions: Pink Profusion is a Chicagoland Grows creeping phlox selected for an especially dense covering of pink flowers each spring, nearly obscuring the low, needle-leaved mat beneath. Plant it in sharply drained soil in full sun to light shade for the heaviest bloom and to avoid winter crown rot. Shear lightly after flowering to maintain a tight, even mat through the growing season.

common_name: Bridal Veil Aromatic Aster (White-Flowered Chicagoland Grows Aster)

planting.note: Plant in average, well-drained soil in full sun in spring, giving the mound room to fill out by fall.

directions: Bridal Veil is a Chicagoland Grows aromatic aster covered in small white daisy flowers over a compact, rounded mound in autumn, offering a clean contrast to the pink and violet tones of its sibling selections. It carries the same heat and drought tolerance typical of the breeding line and needs no staking even in open sites. Grow it in full sun in well-drained soil and cut the mound back hard in late winter.

common_name: Spilled Buttermilk Prairieblues Baptisia (Pale Creamy-Yellow False Indigo)

planting.note: Plant container stock in spring in well-drained soil in full sun on a permanent site, since Baptisia's deep taproot resents later transplanting.

directions: Spilled Buttermilk is a Prairieblues-series false indigo from the Chicagoland Grows program, its soft, creamy-yellow flower spikes a gentler counterpoint to the bolder purples and blues common in the genus. Site it in full sun in well-drained soil on a permanent spot, since its deep taproot makes later moves or division difficult. Once established it needs little beyond an annual late-winter cutback and tolerates drought and poor soil with ease.

common_name: Whitewater Speedwell (White-Flowered Chicagoland Grows Veronica)

planting.note: Plant divisions or container stock in spring in well-drained soil in full sun, giving the low mat room to spread.

directions: Whitewater is a low, spreading Veronica from the Chicagoland Grows program, sending up short spikes of white flowers over a dense mat of foliage in late spring and early summer. Plant it in average, well-drained soil in full sun, where it works well as edging or spilling over a low wall. Divide the mat every few years to refresh the planting and keep it from thinning in the center.

common_name: Commendation Elm (Cold-Hardy Chicagoland Grows Hybrid Shade Tree)

planting.note: Plant nursery transplants in spring in a wide range of soils in full sun, giving the tree an open site away from other shade trees.

directions: Commendation was bred at the Morton Arboretum from a cross of the Accolade elm with field-elm and Siberian-elm parentage, and is distributed through the Chicagoland Grows cooperative as a vigorous, cold-hardy hybrid shade tree. It resists Dutch elm disease and establishes quickly in a wide range of soils, extending the mature canopy profile associated with American elm to sites where that species is at risk from disease. Plant it in full sun with room to develop its arching crown, and water regularly through its first two seasons to speed establishment.

common_name: Danada Charm Elm (Vase-Shaped Chicagoland Grows Hybrid Shade Tree)

planting.note: Plant nursery transplants in spring in a wide range of soils in full sun, with structural pruning in early years to open up narrow branch angles.

directions: Danada Charm arose from open pollination of the Morton Arboretum's Accolade elm and is promoted through the Chicagoland Grows program as a graceful, vase-shaped shade tree with new foliage tinged red on emergence. It carries good resistance to Dutch elm disease and tolerates a broad range of urban soils, recreating much of the classic American elm silhouette. Because its narrow branch angles can be prone to splitting under ice or wind, structural pruning in the tree's early years helps it develop a sturdier framework.

common_name: State Street Maple (Dense Uniform Chicagoland Grows Miyabe Maple)

planting.note: Plant nursery transplants in spring in a wide range of soils in full sun, in a site with room for its broad, uniform canopy.

directions: State Street is a Miyabe maple selection made at the Morton Arboretum and marketed through the Chicagoland Grows program for its dense, symmetrical canopy and tolerance of difficult urban conditions, including compacted and alkaline soils. It is a tougher alternative to more commonly planted maples where road salt, heat, and limited root space are concerns, such as street tree plantings. Plant it in full sun with adequate room for its mature spread, and water consistently through establishment in its first few years.
